models.description: Predicts logP, the log of the octanol-water partition coefficient -- a standard lipophilicity measure.
models.notes: First model wired through this pipeline (see CHEMPROP_INTEGRATION.md) -- this checkpoint was provided pre-trained without accompanying dataset/metrics documentation, so those fields are left null rather than guessed. Architecture and weight-loading were validated against a from-scratch PyTorch/Chemprop reconstruction of this exact checkpoint on 24 diverse test molecules (exact match). Fill in the dataset/metrics fields (or ask Claude to, given the training run details) once you have them -- see validate_registry.py.

models.description: Predicts probability that a molecule is protein-reactive (a covalent modifier / electrophilic warhead), trained as a DMPNN scaffold-split classifier.

metrics.note: These are VALIDATION metrics at the checkpoint epoch (24, matching the 'val_loss=0.06' in the original checkpoint filename) -- not held-out test-set metrics, since test_predictions.csv doesn't include ground-truth labels (only SMILES + predicted probability, so real test-set AUROC/precision/recall/F1 can't be computed from it).

training.dateTrained: 2026-04-26 (inferred from checkpoint file timestamps, not explicitly recorded)

models.notes: Target column was named 'label' in the training CSV (generic, not auto-descriptive) -- the UI shows this model's own displayName instead of the raw property key for that reason. JS port cross-validated against all 6,268 real test-set predictions in test_predictions.csv (not just a hand-picked sanity set): 99.0% match the original PyTorch model to <1e-6, mean abs error 0.00056 across the full set. This surfaced and fixed two real, previously-undetected bugs -- (1) the app's molblock round-trip was dropping the V2000 'either' bond stereo flag on double bonds with genuinely unspecified E/Z geometry (affected push-pull alkene/cyanoacrylamide warheads specifically, this model's own target chemotype, causing near-total prediction inversions on ~3% of the test set before the fix); (2) neutral trivalent boron (boronic acids, boronate esters) was defaulting to sp3 instead of the correct sp2 (boron's empty p-orbital makes it sp2 regardless of conjugation, unlike carbon/nitrogen). Both are fixed in molfile.js and chemprop-features.js respectively and apply to every model using this pipeline, not just this one. ~0.3% of the test set (21/6268) still shows moderate residual error (mean 0.03-0.7), concentrated in explicit chiral centers, defined E/Z double bonds, and boronic acids -- within the documented known-approximation scope (see CHEMPROP_INTEGRATION.md), not yet root-caused further.

models.description: Predicts logS, the log10 of aqueous solubility in mol/L -- a standard solubility measure complementary to logP.

dataset.name: AqSolDB (likely -- not yet confirmed; see notes)

models.notes: Directory name (AqSolDB) and file layout strongly suggest this is trained on Sorkun et al.'s AqSolDB (Sci Data, 2019), but this hasn't been explicitly confirmed yet, and the dataset went through a custom curation pipeline (data-curation.py, preprocess.py, merge.py) before training, so treat the citation as provisional until confirmed and the merge/curation logic is understood -- don't cite as plain AqSolDB without checking what the curation changed. Sanity-checked (not yet validated against ground truth or a real PyTorch reconstruction) on 10 molecules with well-known qualitative solubility: correct ordering throughout (small polar molecules, water, insoluble aromatics, insoluble long-chain alkane), and magnitudes broadly track literature values (benzene -1.50 vs lit. ~-1.64; naphthalene -3.20 vs lit. ~-3.6; hexadecane -7.40 vs lit. ~-8; anthracene -5.28 vs lit. ~-6.9 -- same ballpark and correct ordering, largest single gap of the set). Not yet cross-validated against real test-set predictions the way logP and electrophile-reactivity were -- send config.toml/hparams.yaml/splits.json/test_predictions.csv for that and for real dataset/metrics fields once available.

models.description: Predicts melting point in Kelvin. A genuinely hard QSPR target for a 2D-graph-only model -- real melting point depends heavily on crystal packing and polymorphism, which near-identical 2D graphs (e.g. positional isomers) can differ on wildly.

dataset.name: Jean-Claude Bradley Double Plus Good (Highly Curated and Validated) Melting Point Dataset
dataset.citationFull: Bradley, Jean-Claude; Lang, Andrew; Williams, Antony (2014). Jean-Claude Bradley Double Plus Good (Highly Curated and Validated) Melting Point Dataset. figshare. Dataset. https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.1031638.v1
dataset.splitStrategy: pre-defined train/test split provided with the dataset (train/test column); further internal 90/10 train/val split of the train partition during training

metrics.note: Real held-out test-set metric, taken directly from chemprop train's own logged output (test/mse), not derived or estimated. Best checkpoint at epoch 30 of 50 (val_loss=0.22, in chemprop's internal normalized-target units -- the test/mse above is already correctly inverse-transformed back to real K^2).

models.notes: Sanity-checked against 10 molecules with well-known literature melting points (not this dataset's own ground truth, just a plausibility check): mean abs error 41.4 K, broadly consistent with the real 36.9 K test RMSE above. Water was the largest single outlier (119 K error) -- consistent with the same pattern seen in the logP/logS models, where small inorganic-ish molecules are poorly represented in organic-compound training sets. Values in this dataset are in Kelvin (Celsius-derived, e.g. 450.15 K = 177.00 degC exactly), worth knowing if the UI ever offers a degC display option.

models.description: Predicts per-atom MBIS (Minimal Basis Iterative Stockholder) partial charges via a graph-convolutional electronegativity-equalization model (jthorton/nagl-mbis, built on OpenFF's NAGL). Different architecture from the Chemprop models above -- see notes.
models.notes: This is jthorton/nagl-mbis's own pretrained checkpoint (nagl-v1-mbis-dipole.ckpt), not something trained as part of this project -- reused, not created. Despite the '-dipole' filename, inspected directly and confirmed single-readout (mbis-charges only). Genuinely different architecture from every other model in this registry: node-only GraphSAGE convolution (no bond features enter the convolution at all, confirmed from real NAGL/nagl-mbis source), 19-dim atom features (element/connectivity/ring-size), and a closed-form electronegativity-equalization postprocess that analytically guarantees predicted charges sum to the molecule's total formal charge -- not a plain regression head. Requires explicit hydrogens as real graph nodes (added internally, not something you need to draw) -- this app's other models work directly on the heavy-atom skeleton. VALIDATION: bit-exact confirmed against the real reference implementation. A conda env with a working DGL + naglmbis install was later found on the dev machine, making it possible to run jthorton/nagl-mbis's actual MBISGraphModel.compute_properties() (real DGL SAGEConv, not a reimplementation) directly and diff its output against this project's JS port across 28 molecules -- every element in the trained vocabulary, charged species ([NH4+], carboxylate anion), fused rings, ring sizes 3-6, and degree 1-4 edge cases. Max per-atom charge discrepancy was ~2e-7 (float32 rounding noise), and this same diffing process is what surfaced the '-dipole' checkpoint identity fact above (confirmed by comparing raw state_dict tensors, not assumed).

models.description: Predicts LogVP, the log10 of vapor pressure in mmHg (experimental values collected roughly across 15-30 degC, the source dataset's reporting convention, not a single fixed temperature).

dataset.name: EPA/NICEATM OPERA vapor-pressure endpoint, via gkxiao/vapor-pressure's train/test CSVs
dataset.citationFull: Zang, Q.; Mansouri, K.; Williams, A. J.; Judson, R. S.; Allen, D. G.; Casey, W. M.; Kleinstreuer, N. C. In Silico Prediction of Physicochemical Properties of Environmental Chemicals Using Molecular Fingerprints and Machine Learning. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2017, 57 (1), 36-49. https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jcim.6b00625
dataset.splitStrategy: pre-defined train/test split as published (2034/679); further internal 90/10 train/val split of the train partition during training (RANDOM, chemprop split-sizes=[0.9,0.1,0.0], data-seed=0)

metrics.note: Real held-out test-set metrics (chemprop predict on vp_test.csv, a genuine pre-published test split never seen during training -- 0 SMILES overlap with train confirmed by canonical-SMILES check), computed directly against ground truth, not estimated.

models.notes: Trained end-to-end this session (data fetch -> RDKit validation -> chemprop train -> convert -> JS validation), not a reused/pre-existing checkpoint. JS port cross-validated against all 679 real held-out test-set predictions (not just a hand-picked sanity set), by running this app's actual chemprop-model.js/graph-builder.js/chemprop-features.js/dmpnn.js pipeline headlessly in Node (RDKit.js WASM via @rdkit/rdkit) rather than eyeballing a few molecules in the browser: 675/679 (99.4%) match Chemprop's own Python predictions to <1e-3, mean abs error 0.0018 log units (negligible next to the model's own 0.576 test MAE). This surfaced and fixed one real, previously-undetected bug in chemprop-features.js's guessHybridization(): cumulated double bonds on a single atom (isocyanate/isothiocyanate N=C=O / N=C=S, CS2's S=C=S, allene-type centers) were classified as ordinary sp2 carbonyl-style, when they're actually SP (two independent pi systems only fit a linear/sp center) -- before the fix, 14/679 molecules (2.1%) had this discrepancy, several with >0.4 log-unit error; after, only 4/679 (0.6%) remain, all under 0.5 log units and concentrated in chiral-center/E-Z-adjacent structures already within this pipeline's documented known-approximation scope (see CHEMPROP_INTEGRATION.md). Fixed in chemprop-features.js so it applies to every model using this pipeline, not just this one -- worth spot-checking the other regression models' test sets for isocyanates/thiocyanates/CS2-like fragments if any exist, since none of their prior validations would have exercised this code path.

models.displayName: Carbon acid pKa, C-H bonds (per atom)
models.description: Predicts the pKa of C-H bonds (deprotonation to a stabilized carbanion) per candidate carbon site -- a from-scratch LightGBM/DART regressor trained on jensengroup/pKalculator's published training data (Ree et al., 'pKalculator: A pKa predictor for C-H bonds', ChemRxiv 2024, 10.26434/chemrxiv-2024-56h5h), reproducing their graph-charge-shell descriptor construction but using this app's own NAGL-MBIS partial charges instead of the original method's CM5/GFN1-xTB charges (CM5 needs a real xtb binary subprocess, which has no WASM build and cannot run client-side). See notes for the honest accuracy comparison against the original CM5-based model.

dataset.name: pKalculator training set (Ree et al. 2024)
dataset.size: 759 of 775 molecules (16 dropped: contain Se, Si, or I, outside NAGL-MBIS's trained element vocabulary), 3675 of 4132 candidate C-H sites (outlier=True rows and sites with null/inf QM-derived targets dropped), same molecule-level train(620)/test(155) split the paper itself defines
dataset.splitStrategy: paper-defined molecule-level train/test split (dataset_full.pkl's own train_test column) -- not re-split here

hyperparameters.architecture: LightGBM, DART boosting, 1439 trees (round count picked from a fold1 train/val curve, then retrained on the full official train split)
hyperparameters.descriptor: graph charge shell (n_shells=6, CIP-priority + charge tiebreak sort), 1457 features, built from NAGL-MBIS charges over the full heavy+explicit-H atom graph
hyperparameters.lightgbmParams: num_leaves=868, max_depth=8, learning_rate=0.168, min_data_in_leaf=52, feature_fraction=0.548, bagging_fraction=0.756, bagging_freq=5, max_bin=476, lambda_l1=0.0107, lambda_l2=6.07e-06 -- reused directly from the original paper's own Optuna-tuned DART hyperparameters (params_optuna_dart_reg.pkl), not re-tuned for NAGL charges

models.notes: NOT the original paper's model or weights -- retrained from scratch by this project on the paper's own published dataset (jensengroup/pKalculator's dataset_full.pkl, downloaded from its ERDA sharelink with the user's explicit permission), reusing their descriptor-construction METHOD (graph charge shell, same shell count and CIP-priority sort logic) and their tuned LightGBM/DART hyperparameters, but substituting NAGL-MBIS partial charges for CM5/GFN1-xTB charges because CM5 requires a real xtb binary subprocess (no WASM build exists, cannot run client-side) -- explicitly requested by the project owner after this constraint was identified. HONEST ACCURACY COMPARISON: this model scores MAE=1.40/RMSE=2.49 on the paper's own held-out test split (754 of 789 published test sites -- the gap is sites this conversion had to drop, see dataset size note); the original paper's real CM5/GFN1-xTB-based model reports MAE=1.24/RMSE=2.15 on the same nominal split (789 sites) per the published paper. So this NAGL-based version is measurably (~13-16%) less accurate than the original -- a real, expected cost of swapping a semiempirical-QM-derived charge for a GNN-predicted approximation of one, not a training or porting bug. One intentional algorithmic deviation from upstream's own descriptor code, made because it was a cleaner and equally-arbitrary choice for a freshly-trained model: upstream's CIP-tiebreak code has an indirect index-remapping step that (a) crashes on every currently-installable RDKit version when a block contains 2+ dummy-padding atoms (confirmed by running their unmodified code), and (b) even when it doesn't crash, applies a confusing, seemingly-unintended permutation to charge-tied groups -- this implementation instead does a plain stable-sort-by-charge within each tied-priority run, applied identically in both the Python training pipeline (scripts/convert_pka_lightgbm.py's source pipeline) and the JS inference path (pka-descriptor.js), cross-validated to produce bit-identical descriptors across all 4290 real training sites before training. Requires model/nagl-mbis-charges to be loaded first (pka-model.js throws a clear error naming it if not) -- this is a genuine dependency, not a bug. Only scores carbon atoms bearing at least one hydrogen (implicit or explicit); molecules containing Se, Si, or I cannot be scored at all (NAGL-MBIS's trained element vocabulary is H/C/N/O/F/P/S/Cl/Br). This predicts C-H acidity only -- NOT a general titratable-group (O-H/N-H/etc.) pKa predictor, which is a separate, not-yet-built feature.

models.description: Predicts 13C NMR chemical shift per carbon atom. Trained from scratch by this project on NMRShiftDB2's real experimental, atom-indexed shift data -- not a reused/published checkpoint. Only carbon atoms are annotated (applicableElement gating in chemprop-model.js).

metrics.note: Real held-out test-set metric from chemprop train's own logged test/atom/mse, 50 epochs, no hyperparameter tuning beyond this project's usual hiddenSize=300/depth=3 convention -- a reasonable first-pass result, not optimized further.

models.notes: One of three NMR shift checkpoints (13C/19F/1H) trained together -- see scripts/prepare_nmr_training_data.py and scripts/train_nmr_chemprop.sh for the full data-preparation/training pipeline, and each script's own header comments for two real RDKit round-trip bugs that pipeline's own atom-order self-check caught and fixed (Chem.MolToSmiles(canonical=False) does NOT preserve input atom order on re-parse; default SMILES-parse sanitization silently strips explicit H atoms). A fourth nucleus, 15N, was also trained but deliberately NOT shipped -- NMRShiftDB2 only has 84 15N spectra total (vs. 43258 for 13C), and the resulting checkpoint's real test RMSE was ~164 ppm, unusable.

models.description: Predicts 19F NMR chemical shift per fluorine atom. Trained from scratch by this project, combining NMRShiftDB2's own (small) native 19F records with NMRexp's much larger literature-mined database, restricted to molecules with exactly one reported fluorine shift (unambiguous atom assignment -- see notes). Only fluorine atoms are annotated.

dataset.name: NMRShiftDB2 (969 native records) + NMRexp (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.17296666, single-F molecules only)

metrics.note: Real held-out test-set metric from chemprop train's own logged test/atom/mse. Notably worse than 13C/1H -- NMRexp is LLM-extracted from paper text (not a curated/reviewed database like NMRShiftDB2), and combining two heterogeneous sources (different solvents/referencing conventions not accounted for) likely adds real label noise beyond what a bigger dataset alone would fix.

models.notes: One of three NMR shift checkpoints (13C/19F/1H) trained together -- see nmr-13c's own notes field for the shared pipeline/caveats. NMRexp rows were only used when the paper reported exactly one 19F shift value for the whole molecule (single distinguishable fluorine environment) -- multi-fluorine molecules with several reported shifts were dropped rather than guessing which shift belongs to which F atom (NMRexp's own format doesn't map shifts to specific atoms the way NMRShiftDB2's does).

models.description: Predicts 1H NMR chemical shift, one value per HEAVY atom bearing at least one hydrogen -- the mean of that atom's own attached-proton predictions (see notes: the underlying model genuinely predicts a distinct value per hydrogen atom via an explicit-hydrogen graph, but this app's atom-heatmap UI colors real drawn heavy atoms only, so per-heavy-atom values are aggregated for display). Only heavy atoms with at least one hydrogen are annotated.

metrics.note: Real held-out test-set metric from chemprop train's own logged test/atom/mse, on the underlying per-hydrogen-atom predictions (not the heavy-atom-aggregated display values this app shows) -- a genuinely good result for a first-pass, untuned model.

models.notes: One of three NMR shift checkpoints (13C/19F/1H) trained together -- see nmr-13c's own notes field for the shared pipeline/caveats. This is the only checkpoint trained with chemprop's --add-h (explicit hydrogen graph nodes) and the only one requiring js/chemprop-features-explicit-h.js's separate graph builder at inference time (manifest.graphType='explicit-h'). Training labels were built by broadcasting NMRShiftDB2's heavy-atom-indexed 1H shifts onto each heavy atom's real attached-H nodes -- chemically equivalent protons (e.g. a CH3's three H's) genuinely share one true shift, so this is exact for the common case; diastereotopic (inequivalent) protons reported at different values on the same heavy atom get averaged into one approximate shared label instead of their true distinct values, a real bounded limitation of NMRShiftDB2's atom-indexing convention, not something this pipeline could resolve further. The app's own display then re-aggregates (mean) back down to one value per heavy atom for the same reason, compounding this same approximation, not a new one.

models.description: Total molecular energy from the ANI-2x neural network potential (an 8-model ensemble of atomic-environment-vector + per-element neural networks), for driving 3D geometry optimization. Only supports neutral molecules built from H, C, N, O, F, S, Cl -- not a Chemprop/NAGL-style 2D property prediction, this feeds the 3D viewer's optimizer instead of the properties table.

dataset.citationKey: Devereux et al., J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2020, 16, 7, 4192-4202

hyperparameters.architecture: 8-model ensemble, per-element AtomicNetwork (Linear+TightCELU stacks, element-specific widths), 1008-dim AEV (112 radial + 896 angular)
hyperparameters.aev: ANIRadial (eta=19.7, 16 shifts, cutoff=5.1 A) + ANIAngular (eta=12.5, zeta=14.1, 8x4 shifts, cutoff=3.5 A), cosine cutoff function
hyperparameters.combination: mean of the 8 members' summed-over-atoms energy, plus a per-element self-energy correction

models.notes: This is the standard public ANI-2x release bundled in the torchani Python package (torchani.models.ANI2x()), not something trained as part of this project -- reused, not created. Every numeric constant (AEV cutoffs/eta/shifts, per-element layer shapes, species order, self energies, the species-pair index table) was read directly off the live loaded torchani model by convert_ani2x_checkpoint.py, not transcribed from memory or a paper. VALIDATION: real torchani (same installed package) was run on 10 structurally diverse test molecules spanning all 7 supported elements (alkane/ring, alcohol, amine, sulfide, aromatic-F, aromatic-Cl, thiophene, carboxylic acid, a combined N/O/F/Cl amide, a tert-thiol), computing both total energy and per-atom forces (via torch.autograd.grad) as ground truth, then compared against this JS port's CC.ANI.energyAndForces on the identical coordinates: max energy error 8.7e-5 Hartree (~0.05 kcal/mol) and max force-component error 4.7e-7 Hartree/Angstrom across all 10 -- consistent with float32 weight-storage rounding, not a bug (weights are stored as float32; the reference PyTorch run is also float32 internally). This confirms both the AEV forward pass and the from-scratch analytic backprop (through the AEV formulas and the per-element networks) used to compute forces for geometry optimization, not just the forward energy. See ANI2X_INTEGRATION.md for the full validation writeup and known limitations.

models.description: Predicts a 3D conformer directly from the 2D molecular graph in a single forward pass -- a message-passing GNN encodes the graph, then per-atom local geometry and per-rotatable-bond torsion angles are predicted and assembled into a full structure, without any classical force field. An alternative 3D generation method to the hand-tuned classical force field, selectable from the 3D view panel.

dataset.name: GEOM-Drugs
dataset.citationKey: Ganea, Pattanaik et al., NeurIPS 2021 (GeoMol) -- github.com/PattanaikL/GeoMol

hyperparameters.architecture: two weight-tied 3-round message-passing GNNs (model_dim=50), a per-neighborhood 2-head Transformer encoder for local structure prediction, and per-dihedral-pair MLPs (alpha_mlp/c_mlp) for torsion prediction
hyperparameters.assembly: sequential fragment placement with a gamma-fitted rotation per dihedral pair; rings closed via multi-start traversal + Kabsch-averaging

models.notes: The official drugs checkpoint bundled in the GeoMol repo (trained_models/drugs/best_model.pt), not something trained as part of this project -- reused, not created. Every tensor name/shape/hyperparameter was read directly off the live checkpoint by convert_geomol_checkpoint.py, not transcribed from memory. VALIDATION: run against a live PyTorch instance of the same checkpoint, with the same injected noise vectors, on both a simple acyclic molecule and a 46-atom molecule with two fused aromatic rings and a stereocenter. GNN encoder and local-structure prediction: RMSE ~0.1-1% relative to each tensor's own typical magnitude (consistent with float32 rounding). Torsion prediction: v_star matches to ~2e-9, c_ij to ~0.1% relative. Full assembly (including ring closure): all 48 bonds match ground truth's own bond-length range almost exactly with zero outliers, zero nonbonded clashes, and the aromatic ring came out genuinely planar (not enforced anywhere -- it falls out of correct predictions). See GEOMOL_INTEGRATION.md for the full validation writeup and known limitations (only the drugs checkpoint is converted, not qm9; global_transformer=true checkpoints unsupported).
